facts.text: Eugene Onegin premiered in Moscow on 29 March 1879, conducted by Nikolai Rubinstein.
facts.evidence: The premiere took place on 29 March (17 March O.S.) 1879 at the Maly Theatre, Moscow, conducted by Nikolai Rubinstein

facts.text: Worried about an opera without traditional scene changes, Tchaikovsky wanted maximum simplicity and sincerity, so he entrusted the premiere to Moscow Conservatory students.
evidence: Tchaikovsky worried whether the public would accept his opera, which lacked traditional scene changes
he entrusted the first production to the students of the Moscow Conservatory

facts.text: Tchaikovsky didn’t call it an opera but “lyrical scenes”: selected highlights of Onegin’s life rather than a continuous story.
evidence: there is no continuous story, just selected highlights of Onegin's life

facts.text: The idea came from the singer Yelizaveta Lavrovskaya in May 1877. After a sleepless night, Tchaikovsky embraced it.
evidence: In May 1877, the opera singer Yelizaveta Lavrovskaya spoke to Tchaikovsky
Soon after a sleepless night, Tchaikovsky came to embrace the idea

facts.text: Tchaikovsky thought Pushkin’s novel weak on plot; its strength was its characters, social commentary and beautiful verse.
evidence: Tchaikovsky felt that the novel wasn't particularly strong in plot
The strength of the novel resided in its character development and social commentary

facts.text: The libretto keeps much of Pushkin’s own poetry from his novel in verse.
facts.evidence: very closely follows certain passages in Alexander Pushkin's 1825–1832 novel in verse, retaining much of his poetry

facts.text: Monsieur Triquet’s verses were written by Tchaikovsky’s friend Konstantin Shilovsky.
facts.evidence: Tchaikovsky's friend Konstantin Shilovsky contributed M. Triquet's verses in Act 2, Scene 1

facts.text: Gustav Mahler conducted the Hamburg premiere in 1892. Tchaikovsky called him “simply a genius burning with a desire to conduct”.
evidence: The first performance in Hamburg, on 19 January 1892, was conducted by Gustav Mahler
simply a genius burning with a desire to conduct

facts.text: The Met gave the US premiere on 24 March 1920, but its first performance in Russian came only on 15 October 1977.
evidence: The United States premiere was given on 24 March 1920 at the Metropolitan Opera
The first Russian performance by the Metropolitan Opera was on 15 October 1977.

facts.text: Gremin’s aria “Love knows no age” is partly hummed by characters in Chekhov’s play Three Sisters.
facts.evidence: is partially hummed by the characters of Vershinin and Masha in Anton Chekhov's play Three Sisters

facts.text: The first performance outside Russia was in Prague in 1888, conducted by Tchaikovsky himself.
facts.evidence: The first performance outside Russia took place on 6 December 1888 in Prague, conducted by Tchaikovsky himself
